Ye I kinda have to side with wargrim here on this topic, although it's probably not the right thread for it.

Since the Archon (which is Excel) delivers its data in XML quite readily since Office2010, writing a .NET upload is utterly trivial. It's probably slightly more challenging in php, but I believe Joomla! is .NET anyway.

Really, all you need to do is grab the right XML-ids of the fields you want to export (which should be just the results tab in the Archon) and store them in a database somewhere. Add in some reasonably simple queries to pull the data you want to see and then sort it by whatever sorting algorithm you want and voila, it's done.

It's my understanding that a "team" of people was working on it two years ago, those people then abandoned the project, it took ages for them to get replaced and that team "has been working on the matter" since I last brought it up, which is about 6-7 months ago.

How anyone can take more than a few weeks to code something as trivial as the conversion from a few lines of XML to a viewable website is beyond me, but that's where we're at.

>

Once immediately (and directly to the newly appointed chairman) after the NC meeting all the way back in Paris (EC2010) and once during the EC in Poland last year. Messages.Author: johannes
Messages.Body:
Currently the module is being tested by several persons with real Archon data. If you look inside players ranking (i.e from Paris) you can see that it changes. Of course the results are not definite yet.

Yes, this took a very long time, but apparently there are complexities:

- Archon is not necessarily a 2010 Office file (because not everyone has Office 2010). Older formats are NOT XML and a bitch to parse.
- The integration into Joomla requires specific Joomla knowledge. I coded out a few things in PHP back at the time, which was indeed quick. The integration as a proper Joomla module requires a lot more development time and special knowledge.
- It still took too long, this is a downside when you work with volunteers who sometimes have to stop for months because something happens in their life.

@Santh: well, I honestly overlooked your thread (and apparently everybody else). In case of applying for help sending an email to a NC, IC, prince, anybody is usually better.

@wargrim: My memory is shady when going back to 2011, but did I (personally) turn you down? If yes can you PM me that conversation because it would surprise me. Or tell me who turned you down?

Messages.Author: johannes
Messages.Body: P.S: Joomla is not .NET, but PHP so there is no native component to parse Excel. In fact my research back then came up with nothing usable at all so it had to be done more or less from scratch.

Messages.Author: TryDeflectingThisGrapple

All criticism of where/how this topic got posted or wargrim's language aside, he struck at a matter close to my heart.

Not having a ranking system in place after 2 years is simply shameful. The organization exists specifically to maintain the tournament system. When you follow the "V:EKN" link in the main menu you find the follow:

The V:EKN is the organization responsible for sanctioning and regulating official V:TES tournaments, recording V:TES players' ratings (and rankings), and sponsoring the creation of monthly Clan Newsletters.

Don't get me wrong, getting VTES back in print is a noble goal, which I support completely. As is design/test/punblish for new cards. And it's likely that none of these efforts use the same resources that coding and testing a ratings system use.

Nonetheless, the primary objective of the organization is to administer the ratings system and VEKN has failed miserably here. When an organization (even a volunteer one) can't fulfill it's charter, it should be subject to criticism.

Add my name to the list of folks disappointed by VEKN's failure to uphold its charter.

Darby

Thanks for the response Johannes.

Hope you don't mind me bending your ear for a second here.

In June, Robyn and I spoke about the ratings system. I proposed using a hard start date (a complete reboot of ratings) starting the day that the new system goes live.

This does a few things.

First (and most important) - it avoids all potential problems associated with a massive initial data surge into the system. It will contain the scope of roll-out and make final bug-hunts on the live system much easier.

Second - it circumvents any rating error associated with an incomplete data set from the last 18 months, and puts everyone on an equal footing going forward.

Third - it would allow you to tweak the ratings formula (if desired) without seeing a "step change" in ratings as historical data were re-weighted.

The downside - yes, it penalizes though who have both good past-year tournament performance and responsible organizers. I really hate to see that happen, but the logistical benefits may very well out-weight this (admittedly significant) draw-back.

In either start-up case, we're probably looking at 12-18 months of post-launch data entry just to get back to ratings values that accurately represent performance. Probably would be useful to recognize that.

Just offering something for you to consider as the roll-out date approaches.

Take care,
Darby.

This is already happening in the Formula for finalists. When you submit an Archon it counts the number of players and modifies your finalist ranking bonus based on a logarithm based on 15 (Why seems a little beyond me) so that basically, you get 2log15(Player count) - 1 = multiplier. If you attend a 15 player tournament you'd get 1. If you attended a tournament with 4 players you'd get close to 0. If you attended a tournament with 30 players you'd get about 1.4. If you want to do the calculation on what multiplier you get it isn't too hard.

You could apply it across the board, but really even at the big tournaments everyone gets handed a few 'easy VPs' just as much as you do if you attend frequent events. If you are worried your rating is slipping, travel more OR hassle your local princes into more events.

You have a false dichotomy there.

According to the original  charter , V:EKN is the local volunteers.
According to the current  FAQ , V:EKN is the players.

I'd have outlined much more specific roles and responsibilities if I were going to charter a volunteer organization.

i.e.
National Coordinator - must publicize 1 national tournament per year, and coordinate at least 1 tournament per month, though they need not attend or judge the monthly events, remove dis-functional local coordinators from the lists quarterly, i.e. no local volunteer should be in the list if they don't have a working email address listed and if they haven't performed their specific duties, with the national coordinator to be removed if no events have been run in their country in the last 6 months

Local Coordinator - coordinate at least 1 demo or tournament every 3 months, not necessary to judge or demo themselves, simply to arrange the time/date/location and publicize before and report afterwards

Specialty volunteers - would have specific tasks with public deadlines.

I'm not of the opinion that ranking/ratings adds any real value to the tournament community. Our most recent Atlanta tournament had 15 players, only 3 of whom weren't in the Hall of Fame (4 visiting HoF players from Ohio were in attendance). Does the ratings of those players matter in the slightest? No. Were the games amazingly tense and good because everyone had a clue and knew how to play at the top level? Absolutely.

If V:EKN, i.e. the local volunteers, want rankings and ratings, then they should certainly have it, and they should certainly have a deadline promised and delivered upon by the specialty volunteers that commit to it.

I'd be in favor of scrapping that bit of the charter, as it is simply one more area where failure to follow thru occurs. If you were to go back thru the  Usenet newsgroup , you'd find 12 years of complaints about the system, a significant percentage tied to the website, a significant percentage tied to the formula, and a sizable percentage tied to the failure of the local volunteer to finish their task correctly.

Announcing/publicizing/advertising the events, getting players to attend, running great events and reporting them are the only items I think local volunteers need to concentrate on.

A touch more random Usenet history:
Johannes volunteered database hosting and server space in  2009 . He then made a public call for additional volunteers in  January 2010 .

I think some of the maths on that page isn't correct. Well, it probably is, but the rating point function isn't the right one.

It should be :
[90/30/0]*(2*log(NB_PLAYERS)/log(15)-1+coeff) + 8 * NB_GW + 4 * NB_VP + 5
where [90/30/0] works this way: use 90 for the winner, 30 for finalists, and 0 for non-finalists
NB_PLAYERS is the number of players
NB_GW is the number of Game Wins of the player
NB_VP is the number of Victory Points of the player
coeff is: 0 for standard tournaments, 0.25 for CCQs and Nationals, 1 for Continentals

With this evaluation, I get (for tournament #4 of 2013 and for the winner):
(90 * (2 * log(19) / log(15)) - 1 + 0) + 8 * 3 + 4 * 16 + 5 = 198.7 (should round up to 199).
The page displays  170 . Did you get that value from the Archon, or is it calculated by the server?
